interactions.summary: Jiang restates why categorization is powerful for manipulating the material world and building technology, but insists that imagination and the heart are the only route to the moon’s truth and the universe’s deeper secrets.
The reader continues Beatrice’s line that apparent diversity seems to come from matter that is dense or rare.

Jiang presses the class to reconstruct the most purely logical explanation for lunar dark spots, rejects premature answers about craters and dirt color, and steers a student’s cave image toward the idea of varying depth and density.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang-led classroom exchange with student attempts

claims.claim: Jiang says categorization is powerful because it lets people break the material world into basic elements and manipulate those elements into technology.
Jiang argues that this technological, scientific perspective cannot reveal the truth of the moon, while the heart and imagination can carry a person into the universe’s deeper secrets.
The quoted line frames the dark spots as a problem of apparent diversity that might be explained by matter being dense in some places and rare in others.
claims.temporal_scope: Quoted literary material read aloud on 2026-06-15.

claims.claim: Jiang presents Beatrice’s initial explanation as the straightforward logical account that the moon’s dark patches come from differences in density or rarity.

A student first reaches for material differences such as craters, asteroids, or different substances, but Jiang rejects these as insufficiently basic for the logical structure he is trying to isolate.
A student then proposes a depth-based explanation, comparing the moon’s dark areas to the darkness of a cave that grows deeper farther in.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang gives categorization its due as the engine of technology, then sharply limits its jurisdiction.
signature_moments.source_phrase: categorization allows you to better manipulate the material world
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This keeps the lecture from becoming anti-reason in a naive way; reason is potent, but its potency belongs to control, not ultimate truth.

signature_moments.moment: The moon becomes unreadable to science until the heart is allowed to see it.
signature_moments.source_phrase: that will not let you see the moon
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It preserves Jiang’s striking reversal from astronomical object to spiritually opaque symbol.

signature_moments.moment: Beatrice’s dense-and-rare formula arrives as the clean logical explanation Dante is about to dismantle.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This phrase is the hinge for the next several packets, because Jiang uses it to stage a debate about the limits of material explanation.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang’s name for the truths imagination can reach after logic has exhausted its material utility.
The initial rational explanation for apparent variation in lunar brightness, tied to differing thickness or reflectivity of matter.
Paired with imagination as the faculty that can see truth where logical analysis cannot.

chronology_notes.note: This packet moves the June 15 discussion from abstract method into the concrete logical reconstruction of the moon problem, without adding cross-source chronology pressure.
